info.title: Keep the purpose
info.text:
Start with the problem to solve.

Relevant details depend on the purpose.

A simpler model can still be useful.

Challenge: Why can a map omit carpet patterns?

Carpet patterns do not help identify a route to the library.

info.title: Essential information
info.text:
A loan system must identify the borrower.

It must identify the borrowed item.

It needs enough data to track the loan.

Challenge: Name two details needed to track a camera loan.

Borrower ID and item ID identify who has which camera. The due date helps track returns.

info.title: Remove distractions
info.text:
Not every real-world detail belongs in a model.

Removing detail makes a model easier to use.

Do not remove information needed for accuracy.

Challenge: Why might an icon omit the serial number?

Its purpose is to recognise a camera category. A serial number identifies one particular camera.

info.title: Purpose changes relevance
info.text:
A detail can matter in one task and not another.

A repair system needs different data from a route map.

Explain choices using the stated task.

Challenge: When would a room light fault become relevant?

When planning repairs, the fault and room location help staff repair the correct light.

info.title: Abstraction in software
info.text:
Users can work without knowing every internal detail.

A button can hide several processing steps.

The hidden steps still happen.

Challenge: What does a return button hide from its user?

It hides the detailed steps for finding the loan and updating its stored status.

info.title: Evaluate a model
info.text:
Check whether the model solves the problem.

Add missing relevant details.

Remove detail that only distracts.

Challenge: How should this route map be improved?

Add the connections between rooms so users can plan a route. Textures can be removed.
